# Living Water Pressure Wash Services

> Living Water Pressure Wash Services Ltd. is a pressure washing, sandblasting and surface restoration company serving Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area (Ontario, Canada) since 1998. It cleans and restores residential, commercial, industrial and heritage properties, has completed 7,500+ projects, carries $5M commercial general liability insurance, is WSIB covered and ISSA-GBAC certified, and is rated 4.9/5 on Google.

## Services
- [Residential Power Washing](https://livingwater-pws.com/residential-power-washing/): Living Water cleans the outside of homes across Toronto and the GTA — driveways, interlock, patios, brick, stone, stucco, siding, roofs, decks and fences — using low-pressure soft washing with biodegradable cleaners where high pressure would damage siding, mortar or window seals.
- [Commercial Pressure Washing](https://livingwater-pws.com/commercial-power-washing/): Living Water provides commercial pressure washing across Toronto and the GTA for retail plazas, office buildings, parking lots and garages, schools, restaurants, warehouses and construction sites — removing gum, grease, graffiti and stains while keeping the property open and safe.
- [Industrial Pressure Washing](https://livingwater-pws.com/industrial-power-washing/): Living Water provides industrial pressure washing and hydro jetting across Ontario — cleaning silos and tanks inside and out, manufacturing and food plants, bridges and dams, condenser pipes and heavy equipment — with safety-first planning and 24/7 emergency response.
- [Sandblasting & Media Blasting](https://livingwater-pws.com/sandblasting-services/): Living Water offers mobile dustless sandblasting, wet and dry abrasive blasting, micro blasting, soda blasting and dry ice blasting across Toronto and the GTA to remove rust, scale, paint and epoxy from steel, aluminium, brick, concrete and pools.
- [Brick Cleaning & Paint Removal](https://livingwater-pws.com/brick-cleaning-paint-removal/): Living Water cleans brick and removes paint from interior and exterior masonry across Toronto and the GTA, choosing between chemical cleaning, controlled pressure washing and abrasive blasting after assessing the brick and the coating — so mortar, windows and plants are protected.
- [Historical Remediation](https://livingwater-pws.com/historical-remediation/): Living Water restores historic buildings, statues and landmarks in Toronto and Ontario using heritage-appropriate methods — steam cleaning, soda and micro blasting, wet and dry sandblasting, and lead paint removal — with a working knowledge of the brick, stone and metals used in Canadian construction over the past century.
- [Disaster Restoration](https://livingwater-pws.com/disaster-restoration/): Living Water provides 24/7 disaster restoration across Toronto and the GTA — fire and smoke damage cleaning, water extraction and drying, wind and storm damage securing and repair, and mould remediation — restoring homes and businesses to their pre-loss condition. Emergency line: (647) 833-4343.
- [Elevator Pit Cleaning](https://livingwater-pws.com/elevator-pit-cleaning/): Elevator pit cleaning with Living Water starts at $1,500 for a single pit (up to 4 inches of water), $2,500 for a double, $3,500 for a triple and $4,500 for four pits, each including full cleaning and sanitizing so the pit is ready for paint. Living Water cleans elevator pits for condominium corporations, property managers and commercial buildings across Toronto and the GTA — removing debris, standing water, oil, sludge and sewage, then pressure washing, sanitizing and deodorizing the pit. Work is coordinated with your elevator contractor, scheduled after hours, and documented with before-and-after photos. Emergency line: (647) 833-4343, 24/7.
- [Efflorescence Removal](https://livingwater-pws.com/efflorescence-removal/): Efflorescence is the white, powdery salt deposit left when moisture moves through masonry and evaporates. Living Water removes it from brick, natural stone, concrete and interlock across Toronto and the GTA, and is trusted as the warranty service provider for many Ontario stone manufacturers.
- [Graffiti Removal](https://livingwater-pws.com/graffiti-removal/): Living Water removes graffiti from brick, concrete, stone, metal and glass across Toronto and the GTA — usually within the same week — using bio-friendly chemical removers and controlled pressure washing selected for the surface, and can apply anti-graffiti coatings afterwards.
- [Stone Restoration](https://livingwater-pws.com/stone-restoration/): Living Water cleans and restores natural stone — marble, granite, limestone, sandstone and precast — on homes, commercial buildings and heritage properties across Toronto and the GTA, removing stains, mineral deposits and organic growth with methods matched to the stone.
- [Metal Restoration](https://livingwater-pws.com/metal-restoration/): Living Water restores metal surfaces across Toronto and the GTA — removing rust, oxidation, old paint and coatings from steel, stainless steel, aluminium and copper — using cleaning, sandblasting or media blasting chosen for the metal and the finish required.

## FAQ
**How quickly can Living Water start?**
Residential jobs are usually booked within 2–5 days, and same-week service is standard. Commercial and industrial clients get 24/7 emergency response on (647) 833-4343.

**Are you licensed and insured?**
Yes. Living Water is fully licensed in Ontario, carries $5 million in commercial general liability insurance, is WSIB covered and ISSA-GBAC certified. We send a Certificate of Insurance to your property manager, condo board or HOA on request.

**Will pressure washing damage my driveway, brick or siding?**
Not when it is done right. We match the pressure, nozzle, water temperature and chemistry to each surface — interlock, brick, vinyl, stucco, stone and wood all need different approaches. Where high pressure is wrong we soft wash, steam or use media blasting instead.

**Do you do commercial and industrial work?**
Yes — refineries, plants, silos and tanks, heritage restoration, graffiti removal, sandblasting and elevator pit cleaning. Many of our clients are property managers, general contractors and municipalities. Our crews are certified boom and scissor lift operators.

**What areas do you serve?**
Toronto and the entire Greater Toronto Area, including Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, Markham, Richmond Hill, Oakville, Burlington, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa, plus Hamilton, Niagara, Guelph, Cambridge, Barrie and Simcoe County.

**Is the quote free?**
Yes. Assessments are free and no-obligation, and you receive a fixed written quote before any work starts.

## Expert guides
- [Soft Washing vs Pressure Washing: Which Does Your Property Need?](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/soft-washing-vs-pressure-washing/): Soft washing uses low pressure (similar to a garden hose) plus biodegradable cleaners to kill and dissolve algae, mould and mildew; pressure washing uses high-pressure water — often heated — to physically blast off dirt, oil and stains. Use soft washing on siding, stucco, roofs, painted wood and soft or heritage masonry; use pressure washing on concrete, interlock and other hard, durable surfaces.
- [How to Remove Efflorescence from Brick, Stone & Interlock](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/how-to-remove-efflorescence/): Efflorescence is a white, powdery salt deposit left when water moves through brick, concrete, stone or mortar and evaporates at the surface. Light, fresh efflorescence can be dry-brushed off; established deposits need a masonry cleaner suited to the material, applied to a pre-wetted surface and thoroughly rinsed. It stops returning only when the moisture source is controlled or the material finishes curing.
- [Is Sandblasting Safe for Brick? Media Blasting Options Explained](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/is-sandblasting-safe-for-brick/): Traditional sandblasting with coarse abrasive at high pressure is not safe for most brick — it strips the hard outer face, exposes the soft core to water and freeze-thaw damage, and erodes mortar. Brick can be cleaned or stripped safely with gentler methods: chemical paint strippers, low-pressure micro blasting with fine media, soda blasting, steam, or dry ice blasting, chosen after a test patch.
- [How Often Should You Pressure Wash in Ontario?](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/how-often-to-pressure-wash-ontario/): Most GTA homes should have driveways, walkways and interlock pressure washed once a year — ideally in spring after road salt season — with house siding and roofs soft washed every one to three years as algae appears, and decks cleaned annually before sealing. Commercial entrances, sidewalks and parking areas typically need cleaning monthly to quarterly depending on foot traffic.
- [Elevator Pit Cleaning: What Building Managers Need to Know](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/elevator-pit-cleaning-guide/): Elevator pits collect garbage, dust, oil and water over time, creating fire, slip and environmental hazards for riders and maintenance crews. Building managers should have pits inspected during routine elevator maintenance and professionally cleaned whenever debris, oil, standing water or odours are present — and immediately after flooding or a sewage backup.
- [How to Hire a Pressure Washing Contractor in the GTA: 10 Questions to Ask](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/hiring-a-pressure-washing-contractor/): Before hiring a pressure washing contractor in Ontario, confirm they carry commercial general liability insurance and WSIB coverage (and can send certificates), ask how they will clean each surface and protect plants, windows and runoff, get a fixed written quote with scope and timing, and look for verifiable reviews and before-and-after photos of similar work.
- [Winter Elevator Pit Checklist for Condo & Property Managers](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/winter-elevator-pit-checklist/): In winter, condo and property managers should ask their elevator contractor to report pit conditions at every maintenance visit, watch for water, salt residue, odours and debris, keep entrance matting and sill areas clean to limit meltwater, test sump pumps before the thaw, and book a professional pit cleaning after winter — or immediately after any flood, leak or sewage backup.
- [How to Clean and Re-Sand Interlock Pavers](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/interlock-cleaning-and-resanding/): Interlock is cleaned by pre-treating stains and organic growth, washing with a rotary surface cleaner (not a bare wand) to avoid stripes, flushing out old joint sand and debris, letting the pavers dry completely, then sweeping new polymeric sand into the joints and activating it with a light mist. Sealing is optional and protects colour and helps resist stains.
- [How to Remove Paint from Brick Without Damaging It](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/remove-paint-from-brick/): The safest way to remove paint from brick is a chemical paint stripper matched to the coating, left to dwell (often under a cover), then removed with low-pressure rinsing or scraping — with gentle micro or soda blasting only for stubborn residue. Avoid high-pressure washing and coarse sandblasting, which strip the brick's fired face and lead to water damage.
- [Graffiti Removal Guide: Brick, Concrete, Stone & Metal](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/graffiti-removal-guide/): Graffiti is best removed quickly with a remover matched to the paint and the surface — solvent-based removers for spray paint and markers, followed by controlled low-to-medium pressure rinsing — rather than high pressure alone, which drives paint deeper into porous brick and concrete. Anti-graffiti coatings make future tags much easier to remove.
- [Pressure Washing Cost in Toronto: What Affects the Price](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/pressure-washing-cost-factors/): Pressure washing prices in the GTA depend mainly on the area and type of surface, how heavy the staining or growth is, the cleaning method required (soft wash, hot water, chemical or blasting), access and height (ladders, lifts, containment), extras like re-sanding or sealing, and scheduling such as after-hours or emergency work. A site-specific, fixed written quote is the only reliable number.
- [After a Fire: First Steps for Property Owners](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/fire-smoke-damage-first-steps/): After a fire, wait until the fire department confirms the building is safe to enter, contact your insurance company right away, document the damage with photos before anything is moved, secure the property against weather and entry, and start professional smoke, soot and water clean-up quickly — soot and firefighting water keep causing damage the longer they sit.
- [Pool Shell Sandblasting & Surface Prep: What to Know Before Resurfacing](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/pool-shell-sandblasting-and-prep/): Abrasive blasting strips old paint, coatings, plaster residue and surface contamination from a concrete pool shell so a new finish can bond. It is done with the pool empty, with dust and media contained, and is normally followed by cleaning, repairs and the new surface or coating.
- [Condo Parking Garage Cleaning: Frequency, Methods and Planning](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/condo-parking-garage-cleaning-guide/): Condo parking garages collect road salt, oil and grit that stain concrete, clog drains and track into lobbies. Most buildings schedule a full wash in spring after the salt season, with spot cleaning of oil and drive lanes as needed, planned in zones so residents can still park.
- [Roof Moss Removal in Ontario: Safe Methods and What to Avoid](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/roof-moss-removal-ontario/): Moss and algae on Ontario roofs should be removed with low-pressure soft washing and a roof-safe cleaning solution, never a high-pressure jet, which strips granules and shortens shingle life. Shade, damp and tree debris cause regrowth, so trimming branches and periodic treatment help keep it from returning.
- [Pressure Washing Before Selling Your Home: What to Clean First](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/pressure-washing-before-selling-your-home/): Before listing a home, clean the surfaces buyers see first: the driveway and walkway, front entrance and steps, siding or brick, the patio or deck and any visibly stained roof slopes. Washing is quick, low-cost compared with most pre-sale work, and photographs well, so book it before listing photos.
- [Can You Pressure Wash in Winter in Ontario?](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/winter-pressure-washing-ontario/): Yes, some pressure washing can be done in an Ontario winter, but not every job. Hot-water equipment, sheltered or indoor areas such as garages and elevator pits, and above-freezing days work well. Exterior jobs that would leave water to freeze into ice on walkways are better booked for milder weather.
- [Sandblasting vs Soda Blasting vs Dry Ice Blasting: Which Is Right?](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/sandblasting-vs-soda-vs-dry-ice-blasting/): Abrasive (sand-type) blasting is the most aggressive and suits steel, concrete and heavy coatings. Soda and micro-abrasive blasting are gentler and suit brick, stone and delicate surfaces. Dry ice blasting cleans without leaving media residue and suits equipment and sensitive areas. The right choice depends on the surface and what must come off.
- [Power Washing vs Pressure Washing: What's the Difference?](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/power-washing-vs-pressure-washing/): Pressure washing uses high-pressure water, usually at normal temperature. Power washing uses the same pressure plus heated water, which cuts grease, oil and gum better. Both are used in Toronto, but heated water is not right for every surface, so the method should match the material and the stain.
- [Interlock & Paver Sealing: Finishes, Timing and What to Expect](https://livingwater-pws.com/guides/interlock-paver-sealing-guide/): Seal interlock or pavers only after they are fully cleaned, re-sanded with polymeric sand and completely dry. A natural-look sealer protects with little change in appearance, while an enhanced or wet-look sealer deepens colour. Sealing helps resist stains, salt and weed growth, and needs reapplying every few years depending on sun, traffic and the product.
